chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Makki, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid (from whom he narrated), from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not buy anyone from the Sudan; if it is necessary, then buy from the Nuba, for they are among those of whom Allah the Exalted said: "And among those who say, 'We are Christians,' We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded." Indeed, they will remember that portion, and a group of them will emerge with the Qa'im (peace be upon him) from us.'
And do not marry anyone from the Kurds, for they are a type of Jinn, and Allah has lifted the veil from them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on buying slaves from Sudan and marrying Kurds according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the Nuba people to the Quranic verse 5:13, interpreting their 'forgetting of a portion' as a spiritual state that will culminate in a specific group joining the Awaited Imam (al-Qa'im). He further characterizes the Kurds as a distinct lineage of Jinn whose veil has been lifted, offering a unique cosmological perspective on ethnic identity within Shia eschatology.
